topics.description: End devices, intermediary devices (switches, routers, hubs, modems, access points), protocols (TCP/IP), and guided/unguided transmission media.

topics.title: Types of Networks
topics.description: PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN; Peer-to-Peer vs Client-Server architectures; Bus, Star, Ring, Mesh, and Hybrid network topologies.

topics.title: Advantages and Disadvantages of Network
topics.description: Hardware/software resource sharing, centralized backup, fast communication vs security threats, malware propagation, and setup cost.

topics.title: Unit Summary and Review Exercise
topics.description: Network architecture comparison matrices, topology diagrams, and unit assessment questions.

book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 3: Application Software

topics.title: Using Application Software
topics.description: Overview of general-purpose office productivity suites vs special-purpose software applications.

topics.title: Word Processing
topics.description: Microsoft Word / LibreOffice Writer interface, paragraph formatting, styles, tables, headers/footers, page breaks, and document printing.

topics.title: Manipulating Data in Spreadsheet
topics.description: Workbooks, worksheets, cell references (relative, absolute $A$1), arithmetic formulas, built-in functions (SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX, MIN, IF), and charts.

topics.title: Creating Presentation
topics.description: Slide design principles, slide layouts, master slides, inserting multimedia, slide transitions, custom animations, and slide show delivery.

topics.title: Unit Summary and Review Exercise
topics.description: Office suite shortcut keys, spreadsheet formula exercises, and review questions.

book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 4: Image Processing and Multimedia

topics.title: Image
topics.description: Digital image representation, pixels, spatial resolution (PPI/DPI), raster (bitmap) vs vector graphics, RGB and CMYK color modes, and image file formats.

topics.title: Multimedia Production Planning Strategies
topics.description: Five components of multimedia (text, image, audio, video, animation), storyboarding, scriptwriting, and production workflow.

topics.title: Using Image Processing Software
topics.description: Layers, selection tools (marquee, lasso, magic wand), cropping, transforming, color correction, cloning, filters, and exporting digital graphics.

topics.title: Unit Summary and Review Exercise
topics.description: Image format comparisons, tool icons, and unit review exercises.

book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 5: Information and Computer Security

topics.title: Definition of Security
topics.description: Information security vs computer security, protecting hardware, software, and data assets from unauthorized access.

topics.title: Principles of Computer Security
topics.description: The CIA Triad: Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability; authentication, authorization, and non-repudiation.

topics.title: Computer Security Threats
topics.description: Natural vs human threats; Malware (viruses, worms, Trojans, ransomware, spyware, adware), phishing, and Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks.

topics.title: Potential Losses Due to Security Attacks
topics.description: Data loss, financial theft, identity theft, system downtime, and legal/reputational consequences.

topics.title: Securing Yourself and Your Computer Systems
topics.description: Strong password policies, multi-factor authentication, antivirus software, firewalls, regular backups, and safe browsing.

book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 6: Fundamentals of Programming

topics.title: Defining a Problem and Computational Problem
topics.description: Computational thinking, well-defined problems, identifying Inputs, Processes, and Outputs (IPO model).

topics.title: Steps in Problem Solving
topics.description: Problem definition, problem analysis, algorithm design, coding, testing & debugging, and documentation.

topics.title: Working with Flowcharts and Block Programming
topics.description: Pseudocode, standard flowchart symbols (oval, parallelogram, rectangle, diamond, arrow), sequence/selection/iteration structures, and Scratch block coding.

topics.title: Problem Solving Approaches
topics.description: Top-down modular design, stepwise refinement, and bottom-up problem solving strategies.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 1: The Discipline of History and Human Evolution
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 1: The Discipline of History and Human Evolution

topics.title: Meaning of Prehistory and History
topics.description: Distinction between prehistory (before writing) and history (recorded human past).

topics.title: The Discipline of History
topics.description: Importance of history, primary vs secondary sources, dating techniques (radiocarbon, potassium-argon), periodization, and Ethiopian historiography.

topics.title: The Evolution of Human Beings
topics.description: Scientific theory of evolution, hominid fossil discoveries in the Ethiopian Rift Valley (Ardipithecus kadabba/ramidus, Australopithecus afarensis Lucy/Dinknesh, Homo habilis, Homo erectus, Homo sapiens Idaltu).

topics.title: The Stone Age
topics.description: Paleolithic (Oldowan, Acheulean tools), Mesolithic, and Neolithic Revolution (domestication of plants like teff/enset and animals).

topics.title: The Emergence of States
topics.description: Theories of state formation: agriculture surplus, irrigation management, trade, religion, and military leadership.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 2: Ancient World Civilizations up to c. 500 AD
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 2: Ancient World Civilizations up to c. 500 AD

topics.title: Ancient Civilizations of Africa
topics.description: Ancient Egypt (Nile gift, pharaohs, pyramids, hieroglyphics, mummification) and Kingdom of Kush/Meroe (iron smelting, Meroitic script).

topics.title: Civilizations in Asia
topics.description: Mesopotamia (Sumerians, cuneiform, Code of Hammurabi), Persia, Ancient India (Indus Valley, Hinduism, Buddhism), and Ancient China (Shang, Zhou, Qin, Han, Great Wall, silk, paper).

topics.title: Ancient Civilization of Latin America
topics.description: Maya, Inca, and Aztec civilizations: astronomical calendars, terraced agriculture, and monumental architecture.

topics.title: Civilizations in Europe
topics.description: Ancient Greece (Athens direct democracy, Sparta, philosophy, Olympics) and Ancient Rome (Roman Republic, Roman Empire, Roman law, engineering).

topics.title: Rise and Spread of Christianity
topics.description: Origins in 1st-century Judea, teachings of Jesus Christ, Roman persecution, Emperor Constantine (Edict of Milan 313 AD), and Council of Nicaea.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 3: Peoples and States in Ethiopia and the Horn to the End of 13th C.
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 3: Peoples and States in Ethiopia and the Horn to the End of 13th C.

topics.title: Languages, Religions and Peoples of Ethiopia and the Horn
topics.description: Afro-Asiatic (Cushitic, Semitic, Omotic) and Nilo-Saharan superfamilies; indigenous religions (Waaqeffanna), Judaism, Christianity (Ezana, Nine Saints), and Islam (First Hijra to Aksum in 615 AD).

topics.title: Pre-Aksumite States and Their Geographical Setting
topics.description: Land of Punt (myrrh, gold, ivory trade with Egypt) and Damat (D'mt, Yeha temple, Mukarib title, South Arabian contacts).

topics.title: The Aksumite Kingdom
topics.description: Rise of Aksum, Red Sea international trade at Adulis, coinage (gold, silver, bronze), monolithic stelae, territorial expansion, and causes of decline.

topics.title: The Zagwe Dynasty
topics.description: Mara Teklehaimanot, capital at Roha (Adafa), King Lalibela and the eleven rock-hewn monolithic churches, architectural legacy, and end of Zagwe rule (1270).

topics.title: The Sultanate of Shewa
topics.description: Makhzumite dynasty (founded c. 896 AD), trade routes linking the interior highlands with Zeila, and absorption by the Sultanate of Ifat.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 4: The Middle Ages and Early Modern World, c. 500 to 1750s
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 4: The Middle Ages and Early Modern World, c. 500 to 1750s

topics.title: The Middle Ages in Europe
topics.description: Western European feudalism (lords, vassals, serfs, manorial system), the Catholic Church, the Byzantine Empire (Justinian Code, Constantinople), and the Crusades.

topics.title: The Middle Ages in Asia
topics.description: Rise and expansion of Islam (Prophet Muhammad, Hijra 622 AD, Umayyad and Abbasid Caliphates, Islamic golden age science), Ottoman Empire, and Ming/Tang/Song China.

topics.title: Development of Early Capitalism
topics.description: Growth of medieval towns, merchant and craft guilds, banking (Medici), joint-stock companies, and mercantilism.

topics.title: The Age of Explorations and Discoveries
topics.description: Portuguese and Spanish maritime voyages: Henry the Navigator, Vasco da Gama, Christopher Columbus, Ferdinand Magellan, and global trade shifts.

topics.title: The Renaissance
topics.description: Italian and Northern European Rebirth: humanism, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Shakespeare, Gutenberg printing press, and scientific inquiry (Copernicus, Galileo).

topics.title: The Reformation
topics.description: Martin Luther (95 Theses, 1517), John Calvin, Protestant churches, English Reformation, and the Catholic Counter-Reformation (Council of Trent, Jesuits).

topics.title: Industrial Revolution
topics.description: Origins of the Industrial Revolution in 18th-century Britain: textile mechanization, James Watt's steam engine, coal and iron.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 5: Peoples and States of Africa to 1500
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 5: Peoples and States of Africa to 1500

topics.title: Languages and Peoples of Africa
topics.description: The four major African language superfamilies: Afro-Asiatic, Niger-Congo (including Bantu migrations), Nilo-Saharan, and Khoisan.

topics.title: States in North Africa
topics.description: Fatimid Caliphate in Egypt, Almoravid and Almohad Amazigh (Berber) empires in the Maghreb, and Mamluk rule.

topics.title: Spread of Islam in West Africa
topics.description: Peaceful diffusion of Islam across the Sahara via Amazigh merchants, growth of Islamic scholarship in Timbuktu, Gao, and Kano.

topics.title: States in Western Africa
topics.description: Ancient Ghana (Wagadu), Empire of Mali (Sundiata Keita, Mansa Musa), Songhai Empire (Sunni Ali, Askia Muhammad), Kanem-Bornu, and Hausa city-states.

topics.title: Equatorial, Central and Eastern Africa
topics.description: Kingdom of Kongo, Swahili coastal city-states (Kilwa, Mombasa, Zanzibar, Mogadishu), and Indian Ocean trade.

topics.title: Southern Africa
topics.description: Great Zimbabwe (stone enclosures, gold trade with Sofala), Mutapa (Mwene Mutapa) Empire, and Khoisan/Bantu societies.

topics.title: Intra and Inter-Continental Relations
topics.description: Trans-Saharan gold-salt caravan trade routes and Red Sea / Indian Ocean commercial networks.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 6: Africa and the Outside World 1500–1880s
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 6: Africa and the Outside World 1500–1880s

topics.title: Contact with the Outside World
topics.description: Portuguese coastal forts (Elmina, Mombasa), Ottoman presence in North Africa, and shifting trade patterns.

topics.title: Slavery and the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade
topics.description: Triangular Trade between Europe, West Africa, and the Americas; the Middle Passage; demographic, economic, and political devastation in Africa.

topics.title: The "Legitimate" Trade
topics.description: Abolition of the slave trade in the 19th century and transition to exporting palm oil, groundnuts, ivory, gum arabic, and cloves.

topics.title: The White Settlement in South Africa
topics.description: Dutch East India Company settlement at the Cape (1652), Boers/Afrikaners, Khoikhoi and Xhosa wars, British takeover, the Great Trek, and Zulu resistance under Shaka.

topics.title: European Explorers and Missionaries
topics.description: 19th-century European exploration of African rivers (Mungo Park, David Livingstone, Henry Morton Stanley) and missionary activities as precursors to colonization.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 7: States, Principalities, Population Movements & Interactions in Ethiopia 13th to Mid-16th C.
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 7: States, Principalities, Population Movements & Interactions in Ethiopia 13th to Mid-16th C.

topics.title: The "Solomonic" Dynasty & the Christian Kingdom, 13th–16th C.
topics.description: Yekuno Amlak (1270), Kibre Negest ideology, roving royal capitals, Amba Gishen royal prison, territorial expansion under Amde Tsiyon and Zara Yaqob.

topics.title: The Muslim Principalities
topics.description: Zeila trade route and rise of Muslim sultanates: Ifat (Walasma dynasty), Hadiya, Fatagar, Dawaro, Bali, Mora, Adal.

topics.title: Relationship Between the Christian Kingdom and the Sultanate of Adal, 1520s–1559
topics.description: Rivalry over control of the Zeila trade route, Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi (Ahmad Gragn), Battle of Shimbra Kure (1529), Portuguese and Ottoman intervention, Battle of Woina Dega (1543).

topics.title: Political and Socio-Economic Conditions of Southern and Central States in Ethiopia
topics.description: Kingdoms of Enarya, Bizamo, Damot, Wolaita (Kawo), Kafa (Tato), Yem, Gamo, Hadiya, Dawuro, and Kambata.

topics.title: Population Movements, Expansion and Integration in Ethiopia
topics.description: Argobba, Afar, and Somali movements; the 16th-century Oromo population movement, causes, directions, and Barentu/Borana confederacies.

topics.title: Gadaa System of the Oromo
topics.description: Age-grades, 8-year democratic power transfer, Chaffe assembly, Abba Bokku, Abba Dula, Qallu institution, Siqqee women's rights, and Moggasa/Guddifacha integration.

topics.title: Moggasa and Guddifacha & Egalitarian Systems of Governance
topics.description: Social cohesion mechanisms and indigenous egalitarian governance systems (Sidama Luwa, Gedeo Baalle, Konso Xora, Burji, Nuer, Anuak).

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 8: Political, Social and Economic Processes in Ethiopia Mid-16th to Mid-19th C.
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 8: Political, Social and Economic Processes in Ethiopia Mid-16th to Mid-19th C.

topics.title: Peoples and States of the Eastern, Central, Southern and Western Regions
topics.description: Emirate of Harar (Amir Nur, Jugol wall), Afar Sultanates (Awssa), Somali, Gurage, Silt'e, Hadiya, Kambata, Wolaita, Kafa, Gibe Oromo Monarchies (Jimma, Limmu-Enarya, Gumma, Gomma, Gera), Leqa-Naqamte, Leqa-Qellam, Sheikhdoms of Assosa/Bela Shangul/Khomosha, and Nilotic communities.

topics.title: Gondarine Period (1636–1769)
topics.description: Susenyos and Catholic interlude, Emperor Fasilides' Closed-Door Policy and founding of Gondar (1636), Fasil Ghebbi castles, Iyasu I, Empress Mentewab, urban commerce, and religious debates.

topics.title: The Zemene-Mesafint (1769–1855)
topics.description: Era of the Princes triggered by Ras Mikael Sehul (1769); regional warlordism, decline of imperial authority, devastation of peasantry, and Battle of Debre Abbay (1831).

topics.title: The Yejju Dynasty
topics.description: Ali Gwangul (Ali I), capital at Debre Tabor, Ras Gugsa Merso, and Yejju regency (Enderase) over the Gondarine puppet emperors.

topics.title: The Kingdom of Shewa
topics.description: Founded by Negasi Kristos in Menz; autonomous consolidation under Sahle Selassie (1813–1847), stability, trade, and foreign diplomacy.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 9: The Age of Revolutions 1750s to 1815
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 9: The Age of Revolutions 1750s to 1815

topics.title: Industrial Capitalism in Europe
topics.description: Factory system, steam power, railway revolution, urbanization, rise of industrial bourgeoisie and proletariat working class.

topics.title: The French Revolution (1789–1799)
topics.description: Old Regime Three Estates, Enlightenment ideas (Montesquieu, Voltaire, Rousseau), Storming of the Bastille (July 14, 1789), Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen, Jacobin Reign of Terror, and abolition of feudalism.

topics.title: The Napoleonic Era (1799–1815)
topics.description: Rise of Napoleon Bonaparte, Napoleonic Code, Continental System, spread of revolutionary reforms across Europe, Russian campaign (1812), and Battle of Waterloo (1815).

topics.title: American War of Independence
topics.description: Thirteen British colonies, "No taxation without representation," Stamp Act, Boston Tea Party, Declaration of Independence (July 4, 1776, Thomas Jefferson), George Washington, Treaty of Paris (1783), and US Constitution.

topics.title: The Congress of Vienna (1814–1815)
topics.description: Metternich, Castlereagh, Talleyrand; principles of Legitimacy, Balance of Power, and Compensation; redrawing the map of Europe.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815–1914
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 1: Development of Capitalism and Nationalism 1815–1914

topics.title: Features of Capitalism
topics.description: Private ownership of means of production, free market competition, profit motive, wage labor, and Second Industrial Revolution (steel, electricity, chemicals, petroleum).

topics.title: Features of Nationalism and Formation of Nation States
topics.description: Factors promoting 19th-century nationalism: shared language, history, culture, territory, and reaction against Napoleonic/dynastic rule.

topics.title: Unification of Italy
topics.description: Risorgimento leaders: Giuseppe Mazzini (Young Italy), Count Camillo di Cavour (Piedmont-Sardinia diplomacy), Giuseppe Garibaldi (Red Shirts), and King Victor Emmanuel II (1861–1870).

topics.title: Unification of Germany
topics.description: Zollverein customs union, Otto von Bismarck's "Blood and Iron" Realpolitik, Danish War (1864), Austro-Prussian War (1866), and Franco-Prussian War (1870–71).

topics.title: The American Civil War (1861–1865)
topics.description: Conflict between industrial North (Union) and plantation slave-owning South (Confederacy); Abraham Lincoln, Homestead Act, Emancipation Proclamation (1863), and 13th/14th/15th Amendments.

topics.title: Nationalism and the "Eastern Question"
topics.description: Decline of the Ottoman Empire ("Sick Man of Europe"), Balkan nationalist uprisings (Greece, Serbia, Bulgaria, Romania), Crimean War, and Balkan Wars (1912–1913).

book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 2: Africa & the Colonial Experience (1880s–1960s)

topics.title: General Background to Colonialism
topics.description: Transition from "legitimate trade" and coastal outposts to full-scale imperial partition of Africa.

topics.title: The Motives of European Colonialism
topics.description: Economic demand for raw materials, captive markets, investment outlets, strategic waterways (Suez Canal), and "Civilizing Mission" ideology.

topics.title: Scramble for Africa and the Berlin Conference (1884–1885)
topics.description: King Leopold II in Congo, Anglo-French rivalry, Otto von Bismarck, and the Berlin Conference "Principle of Effective Occupation".

topics.title: Colonial Policies and Administration
topics.description: Company Rule, British Indirect Rule (Lord Lugard), French Direct Rule (Assimilation and Association), Settler Rule, and Divide-and-Rule.

topics.title: Early African Resistance Movements Against Colonialism
topics.description: Samori Toure (Mandinka Empire), Ashanti resistance (Yaa Asantewaa), Maji-Maji Rebellion (Tanganyika), Urabi Pasha (Egypt), Mahdist Sudan, and Herero-Nama uprising.

topics.title: Impacts of Colonial Rule on Africa
topics.description: Arbitrary borders, loss of sovereignty, monocrop cash-crop dependency, land alienation, and infrastructure built solely for resource extraction.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 3: Social, Economic & Political Developments in Ethiopia Mid-19th C. to 1941
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 3: Social, Economic & Political Developments in Ethiopia Mid-19th C. to 1941

topics.title: Long Distance Trade & Cottage Industry in Ethiopia in the 19th Century
topics.description: Jabarti and Afqala merchants, trade routes linking Bonga/Jimma to Massawa, Zeila, Berbera, and Metemma; Maria Theresa Thaler and amole salt bars; cottage crafts (smithing, weaving, pottery, tanning).

topics.title: The Making of the Modern Ethiopian State 1855–1913
topics.description: Emperor Tewodros II (ending Zemene-Mesafint, Gafat Sebastopol, Maqdala 1868), Tekle Giyorgis II, Yohannes IV (Liche Agreement 1878, Boru Meda Council), and Menelik II (territorial incorporation, founding of Addis Ababa 1886, modernization, 1907 Ministerial Cabinet).

topics.title: External Aggressions and the Struggle for the Defense of National Sovereignty, 1871–1896
topics.description: Egyptian invasions defeated at Gundet (1875) and Gura (1876); Hewett (Adwa) Treaty (1884); Mahdist battles (Kufit, Metemma 1889); Italian encroachment, Dogali (1887), Treaty of Wuchale (Article XVII), and the historic Victory of Adwa (March 1, 1896).

topics.title: Inception of Power Struggle Among the Ruling Elites, 1906–1935
topics.description: Empress Taytu Bitul, Lij Iyasu's reforms, 1916 coup and Battle of Segele, Dual Rule (Diarchy) of Empress Zewditu and Regent Ras Tafari Makonnen, and coronation of Emperor Haile Selassie I (1930) & 1931 Constitution.

topics.title: Fascist Italian Aggression and Patriotic Resistance (1935–1941)
topics.description: Walwal Incident (1934), Northern and Southern Fronts (Amba Aradom, Tembien, Maychew, Qorahe, Genale Dorya), Italian East Africa (AOI), Graziani Massacre (Yekatit 12, 1937), Black Lions, Abune Petros, Patriots (Arbegnoch) & Women Patriots, and 1941 Liberation Campaign (Gideon Force).

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 4: Society and Politics in the Age of World Wars 1914–1945

topics.title: The First World War: Causes, Course and the Consequence (1914–1918)
topics.description: MAIN causes (Militarism, Alliances: Triple Entente vs Triple Alliance, Imperialism, Nationalism), Sarajevo assassination, Western/Eastern fronts, US entry, and Treaty of Versailles (1919).

topics.title: The October 1917 Russian Revolution: Cause, Course and Results
topics.description: Tsarist autocracy, 1905 Revolution, February 1917 Revolution, Vladimir Lenin and the Bolsheviks ("Peace, Land, and Bread"), October Revolution, Civil War (Reds vs Whites), NEP, and Stalin's Five-Year Plans.

topics.title: The League of Nations & the Worldwide Economic Crisis
topics.description: Structure and weaknesses of the League of Nations; the 1929 Wall Street Crash and the Great Depression.

topics.title: The Rise of Fascism in Italy, Nazism in Germany and Militarism in Japan
topics.description: Benito Mussolini's March on Rome (1922), Adolf Hitler's Nazi regime (1933), and Japanese militarist expansion into Manchuria (1931) and China (1937).

topics.title: The Second World War: 1939–45
topics.description: Appeasement (Munich Agreement), invasion of Poland (Sept 1, 1939), Axis vs Allies, Battle of Britain, Operation Barbarossa, Pearl Harbor, Stalingrad, El Alamein, D-Day, the Holocaust, and Hiroshima/Nagasaki.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 5: Global and Regional Developments Since 1945
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 5: Global and Regional Developments Since 1945

topics.title: The United Nations Organization: Formation, Mission, Principles and Achievements
topics.description: San Francisco Conference (1945), General Assembly, Security Council (5 permanent veto members), Secretariat, ICJ, and specialized agencies (WHO, UNESCO, UNICEF).

topics.title: The Rise of the Superpowers and the Beginning of the Cold War
topics.description: US-Soviet ideological rivalry, Iron Curtain, Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, Berlin Blockade, NATO (1949) vs Warsaw Pact (1955), arms race, space race, and Cuban Missile Crisis (1962).

topics.title: Situations in Asia During the Cold War: Japan, Korea, China, Vietnam
topics.description: Post-WWII reconstruction of Japan, 1949 Chinese Revolution (Mao Zedong), Korean War (1950–53), and Vietnam War (Ho Chi Minh, Dien Bien Phu, US withdrawal 1973–75).

topics.title: The Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) & the Arab-Israeli Conflict
topics.description: Bandung Conference (1955) and Belgrade (1961); Zionism, 1947 UN Partition of Palestine, 1948 War, 1956 Suez Crisis, 1967 Six-Day War, 1973 Yom Kippur War, and Camp David Accords.

topics.title: The Collapse of the Soviet Union
topics.description: Mikhail Gorbachev's Glasnost (openness) and Perestroika (restructuring), 1989 fall of the Berlin Wall, and 1991 dissolution of the USSR.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 6: Ethiopia: Internal Developments and External Influences from 1941 to 1991
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 6: Ethiopia: Internal Developments and External Influences from 1941 to 1991

topics.title: Major Post-Liberation Administrative Reforms & Socio-Economic Conditions
topics.description: Anglo-Ethiopian Agreements (1942, 1944), Point Four & Ethio-US alliance (Kagnew Station), 1952 Federation and 1962 union of Eritrea, 1955 Revised Constitution, education expansion (UCAA/HSIU), and feudal land tenure (Gebbar/Chisegna).

topics.title: Early Opposition Movements Against the Imperial Rule
topics.description: 1943 Woyane Rebellion, 1960 Abortive Coup (Mengistu and Germame Neway), Bale Peasant Rebellion (Waqqo Gutu), Gojjam Peasant Rebellion (1968), Macha-Tulama Association (Tadesse Birru), Eritrean armed struggle, and the Ethiopian Student Movement ("Land to the Tiller").

topics.title: The Ethiopian Revolution and the Fall of the Monarchy
topics.description: 1973 Wollo famine, February 1974 popular uprisings, formation of the Derg, deposition of Haile Selassie (Sept 12, 1974), Zemacha, 1975 Rural and Urban Land Nationalization Proclamations, and the Red Terror (1977–78).

topics.title: The Ethio-Somalia War, Question of Eritrea, and the Fall of the Derg
topics.description: 1977–78 Ogaden War (Karamara victory), 1984–85 famine and resettlement/villagization, 1987 PDRE Constitution, Battle of Afabet and Shire, and May 1991 collapse of the Derg regime.

book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 7: Africa Since 1960

topics.title: Rise of Independent States in Africa
topics.description: National liberation across North, West (Kwame Nkrumah in Ghana 1957, Guinea 1958, "Year of Africa" 1960), East (Mau Mau in Kenya, Julius Nyerere in Tanzania), and Lusophone/Southern Africa (Algerian FLN, Angola MPLA, Mozambique FRELIMO, Zimbabwe 1980).

topics.title: Struggle Against Apartheid, Pan-Africanism and the OAU
topics.description: Casablanca vs Monrovia blocs, founding of the Organization of African Unity (OAU) in Addis Ababa (May 25, 1963), transformation into the African Union (AU, 2002), and anti-Apartheid victory in South Africa (ANC, Nelson Mandela, 1994).

topics.title: Struggle for Economic Independence
topics.description: Neo-colonialism, structural adjustment programs, Lagos Plan of Action, NEPAD, and Regional Economic Communities (ECOWAS, COMESA, SADC, EAC, IGAD).

topics.title: Major Issues in Contemporary Africa
topics.description: Military coups, ethnic conflicts (1994 Rwandan genocide), external debt, poverty, HIV/AIDS, climate change, and democratization.

book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 8: Post-1991 Developments in Ethiopia

topics.title: The Transitional Government of Ethiopia (TGE) and the 1995 Constitution
topics.description: July 1991 Peace and Democracy Conference, Transitional Charter, 1993 Eritrean Referendum, and the 1995 FDRE Constitution establishing multinational federalism.

topics.title: Hydro-Political History of the Nile (Abay) Basin and Development Issues
topics.description: Colonial-era 1929 and 1959 Nile treaties excluding Ethiopia, Nile Basin Initiative (NBI), Cooperative Framework Agreement (CFA), and the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD, launched 2011).

topics.title: Development Achievements & Challenges of Democratization
topics.description: Infrastructure expansion (roads, universities, telecom, railways, industrial parks), poverty reduction, 1998–2000 Ethio-Eritrean War (Algiers Agreement) & 2018 Peace Accord, and ongoing democratization reforms.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 9: Indigenous Knowledge and Heritages of Ethiopia
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 9: Indigenous Knowledge and Heritages of Ethiopia

topics.title: Indigenous Knowledge and Its Role in Sustainable Development
topics.description: Characteristics of Ethiopian indigenous knowledge: traditional medicine, weather forecasting, soil/water conservation (Konso terracing), social welfare (Iddir, Iqub, Debo/Jigie), and conflict resolution.

topics.title: Heritages of Ethiopia
topics.description: Tangible and intangible UNESCO World Heritage sites of Ethiopia: Rock-Hewn Churches of Lalibela, Simien Mountains, Fasil Ghebbi, Aksum, Lower Valley of the Awash & Omo, Tiya, Harar Jugol, Konso Cultural Landscape, Bale Mountains, Gedeo Cultural Landscape, Meskel, Fichee-Chambalaalla, Gadaa System, Timket, and Shuwalid.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 1: Vegetable, Fruit, and Root Crop Production (Horticulture)
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 1: Vegetable, Fruit, and Root Crop Production (Horticulture)

topics.title: Principles of Horticultural Crop Production and Site Selection in Ethiopia
topics.description: Climatic and edaphic requirements for vegetables, fruits, and root/tuber crops across Ethiopian agro-ecologies.

topics.title: Nursery Establishment, Propagation, Grafting, and Transplanting
topics.description: Seedbed preparation, sexual vs asexual propagation (cuttings, budding, grafting, tissue culture), and hardening off.

topics.title: Post-Harvest Handling, Cold Chain Storage, and Value Addition
topics.description: Physiological maturity vs commercial ripeness, precooling, grading, packaging, and minimizing post-harvest loss.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 2: Coffee, Tea, Spices, and Stimulant Crop Agronomy
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 2: Coffee, Tea, Spices, and Stimulant Crop Agronomy

topics.title: Coffee (Coffea arabica) Genetic Diversity, Ecology, and Shade Management
topics.description: Forest, semi-forest, garden, and plantation coffee systems; pruning, stumping, and Coffee Berry Disease (CBD) control.

topics.title: Coffee Processing (Washed vs. Sun-Dried), Cupping Quality, and ECX Grading
topics.description: Wet pulping, fermentation, parchment drying on raised beds, dry hulling, and specialty export traceability.

topics.title: Agronomy of Tea, Korarima, Ginger, Turmeric, and Black Cumin
topics.description: Acidic highland soils for Camellia sinensis (Wushwush, Gumaro), rhizome curing, and essential oil extraction.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 3: Ruminant, Camel, and Equine Production & Health Management
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 3: Ruminant, Camel, and Equine Production & Health Management

topics.title: Dairy and Beef Cattle Genetic Improvement, Feedlot Fattening, and Ration Formulation
topics.description: Indigenous Boran, Fogera, Horro, and Begait breeds; exotic Holstein-Friesian crossbreeding and Pearson Square rations.

topics.title: Camel and Equine Husbandry in Ethiopian Arid and Highland Agro-Ecologies
topics.description: Physiological drought adaptations of dromedary camels, milk production, and draft animal welfare.

topics.title: Major Transboundary Animal Diseases, Biosecurity, Vaccination, and Veterinary Care
topics.description: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), anthrax, blackleg, CBPP, trypanosomiasis (tsetse vector), and quarantine protocols.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 4: Poultry, Fishery, Aquaculture, and Sericulture
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 4: Poultry, Fishery, Aquaculture, and Sericulture

topics.title: Commercial Layer and Broiler Poultry Housing, Hatchery, and Biosecurity
topics.description: Deep litter vs cage systems, incubation temperature (37.5°C) and humidity, brooding, and Newcastle disease vaccination.

topics.title: Capture Fisheries and Aquaculture in Ethiopian Lakes and Reservoirs
topics.description: Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), African catfish, pond fertilization, dissolved oxygen management, and sustainable catch.

topics.title: Modern Apiculture (Beekeeping) and Silk Production (Sericulture)
topics.description: Transitional Kenya Top Bar and modern Zander frame hives, queen rearing, mulberry/castor silkworm rearing, and cocoon reeling.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 5: Climate-Smart Agriculture, Agroforestry, and Mechanization
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 5: Climate-Smart Agriculture, Agroforestry, and Mechanization

topics.title: Climate Change Adaptation, Conservation Agriculture, and Green Legacy Agroforestry
topics.description: Minimum tillage, permanent organic mulch cover, alley cropping with Faidherbia albida, and carbon sequestration.

topics.title: Precision Irrigation Systems (Drip, Sprinkler), Water Harvesting, and Soil Salinity
topics.description: Water-use efficiency calculations, leaching requirement for saline Rift Valley soils, and night-storage reservoirs.

topics.title: Farm Mechanization, Renewable Bioenergy (Biogas), and Digital Agriculture
topics.description: Tractor implements, combine harvesters, anaerobic digestion of animal manure (CH4 biogas + bioslurry), and satellite advisories.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 6: Agribusiness Management, Agricultural Marketing, and Food Security
book_chapters.description: Curriculum Unit 6: Agribusiness Management, Agricultural Marketing, and Food Security

topics.title: Farm Records, Cost-Benefit Analysis, Depreciation, and Farm Budgeting
topics.description: Fixed vs variable farm costs, gross margin analysis, break-even yield, straight-line depreciation, and balance sheets.

topics.title: Agricultural Value Chains, Cooperatives, Commodity Exchanges (ECX), and Export Trade
topics.description: Producer-processor-exporter linkages, warehouse receipt systems, cooperative bargaining power, and sanitary standards.

topics.title: National Food Security Policies, Nutrition-Sensitive Agriculture, and Entrepreneurship
topics.description: Four pillars of food security (availability, access, utilization, stability), biofortified crops, and youth agribusiness.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 1: Molecular Genetics and DNA Technology
book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 1: Molecular Genetics and DNA Technology covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: DNA Molecular Structure and Semiconservative Replication
topics.description: Watson-Crick double helix model, antiparallel strands (5' to 3' and 3' to 5'), nucleotide units (deoxyribose, phosphate, purine/pyrimidine bases), Chargaff's rules (%A=%T, %G=%C); Semiconservative replication: Helicase, DNA polymerase, RNA primase, Okazaki fragments, and DNA ligase.

topics.title: Transcription and Post-Transcriptional RNA Processing
topics.description: Central dogma of molecular biology; RNA structure vs DNA; Transcription by RNA Polymerase binding promoter region; Template strand reading 3' to 5', mRNA synthesis 5' to 3'; Eukaryotic RNA processing: 5' capping, 3' poly-A tailing, splicing out non-coding introns by spliceosomes.

topics.title: The Genetic Code, Translation and Protein Synthesis
topics.description: Features of the genetic code (triplet, universal, degenerate/redundant, non-overlapping, start codon AUG, stop codons UAA, UAG, UGA); tRNA structure and anticodon loop; Ribosome structure (A, P, E sites); Translation stages: Initiation, Elongation (peptide bond formation), Termination.

topics.title: Recombinant DNA Technology, PCR and Biotechnology Applications
topics.description: Restriction endonucleases ("molecular scissors" cutting palindromic recognition sequences), DNA ligase, plasmid vectors, bacterial transformation; Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR: Denaturation, Annealing, Extension); Gel electrophoresis; Applications in Ethiopian agriculture (tissue culture of teff, coffee) and medicine (recombinant insulin).

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 2: Mendelian Genetics and Inheritance Patterns
book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 2: Mendelian Genetics and Inheritance Patterns covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Mendelian Genetics: Monohybrid and Dihybrid Crosses
topics.description: Mendel's experiments on Pisum sativum; Law of Segregation (alleles separate during meiosis, monohybrid 3:1 phenotypic and 1:2:1 genotypic ratios); Law of Independent Assortment (unlinked genes assort independently, dihybrid 9:3:3:1 ratio); Test cross with homozygous recessive.

topics.title: Non-Mendelian Patterns of Inheritance
topics.description: Incomplete dominance (intermediate heterozygote phenotype 1:2:1 ratio, e.g. Snapdragon flowers); Codominance (both alleles expressed simultaneously, e.g. sickle cell trait HbA/HbS, MN blood group); Multiple alleles (ABO blood group system with IA, IB, i); Polygenic quantitative traits (skin color, human height).

topics.title: Sex Determination, Sex-Linkage and Pedigree Analysis
topics.description: Chromosomal sex determination (XX/XY in humans, ZW/ZZ in birds); Sex-linked inheritance of X-linked recessive traits (Hemophilia A, Red-green color blindness); Hemizygous males (XY) expressing recessive alleles; Interpreting human pedigree charts (autosomal dominant/recessive vs X-linked).

topics.title: Mutations and Chromosomal Abnormalities
topics.description: Gene/point mutations (silent, missense, nonsense, frameshift insertions/deletions); Mutagenic agents (UV, ionizing radiation, chemicals); Chromosomal structural alterations (deletion, duplication, inversion, translocation); Numerical aneuploidy due to nondisjunction during meiosis (Down syndrome Trisomy 21, Turner syndrome XO, Klinefelter syndrome XXY).

book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 3: Evolution and Speciation covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Empirical Evidence for Evolutionary Change
topics.description: Paleontological fossil record and transitional fossils (e.g. Archaeopteryx, Lucy/Australopithecus afarensis discovered in the Afar Depression of Ethiopia); Comparative anatomy: Homologous structures (divergent evolution) vs Analogous structures (convergent evolution), vestigial structures; Biochemical and DNA sequence homology.

topics.title: Theories of Evolution: Lamarckism vs. Darwinian Natural Selection
topics.description: Lamarck's theory of inheritance of acquired characteristics and disuse; Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace: Overproduction, struggle for existence, variation within populations, differential survival and reproduction ("survival of the fittest"); Modern evolutionary synthesis combining Mendelian genetics with natural selection.

topics.title: Population Genetics and the Hardy-Weinberg Principle
topics.description: Gene pool, allele frequency (p + q = 1) and genotype frequency (p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1); Five conditions for Hardy-Weinberg genetic equilibrium (large population, random mating, no mutation, no gene flow/migration, no natural selection); Evolutionary forces disrupting equilibrium: Genetic drift (bottleneck and founder effects), gene flow, natural selection.

topics.title: Speciation Mechanisms and Ethiopian Endemic Biodiversity
topics.description: Biological species concept; Reproductive isolating mechanisms: Prezygotic (temporal, behavioral, ecological, mechanical, gametic isolation) and Postzygotic (hybrid inviability, hybrid sterility); Allopatric speciation via geographical barriers vs Sympatric speciation (polyploidy); Adaptive radiation of Ethiopian highlands endemic wildlife (Walia Ibex, Ethiopian Wolf, Gelada Baboon).

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 4: Human Physiology and Defence Mechanisms
book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 4: Human Physiology and Defence Mechanisms covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Neural Coordination: Action Potentials and Synaptic Transmission
topics.description: Structure of sensory, relay, and motor neurons; Resting membrane potential (-70 mV maintained by Na+/K+ ATPase pump: 3 Na+ out, 2 K+ in); Action potential phases: Depolarization (voltage-gated Na+ channels open, potential reaches +30 mV), Repolarization (K+ channels open), Hyperpolarization, Refractory periods; Saltatory conduction in myelinated axons; Synaptic transmission via neurotransmitter acetylcholine release.

topics.title: Endocrine Coordination and Homeostatic Feedback Loops
topics.description: Ductless endocrine glands and hormone signaling; Hypothalamus-pituitary axis; Blood glucose regulation by pancreatic islets: Beta cells secrete insulin (promotes glycogenesis and glucose uptake), Alpha cells secrete glucagon (stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis); Thyroid hormones T3/T4 and metabolic rate; Adrenal stress hormones (adrenaline and cortisol); Negative feedback control.

topics.title: The Human Immune System and Defence Mechanisms
topics.description: Innate (non-specific) immunity: Physical/chemical barriers (skin, lysozyme, stomach acid), phagocytes (macrophages, neutrophils), inflammatory response, fever; Adaptive (specific) immunity: Humoral response mediated by B-lymphocytes and antibodies (IgG, IgM, IgA, IgE), Cell-mediated response mediated by cytotoxic T-cells (CD8+) and helper T-cells (CD4+); Active vs passive immunity, vaccination mechanisms.

topics.title: Major Pathogenic Diseases and Public Health in Ethiopia
topics.description: Malaria: Plasmodium falciparum lifecycle between female Anopheles mosquito vector and human host (liver and red blood cell phases), symptoms, Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT); Tuberculosis: Mycobacterium tuberculosis pathogenesis, BCG vaccination, DOTS treatment program; HIV/AIDS: Retrovirus replication cycle, reverse transcriptase, destruction of CD4+ T-helper cells, Antiretroviral therapy (ART); Schistosomiasis lifecycle with freshwater snail intermediate host.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 5: Applied Ecology and Environmental Conservation
book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 5: Applied Ecology and Environmental Conservation covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Ecosystem Dynamics, Trophic Levels and Energy Flow
topics.description: Ecosystem components (biotic communities and abiotic factors); Trophic levels: Primary producers (autotrophs), primary consumers (herbivores), secondary/tertiary consumers (carnivores), decomposers; Unidirectional energy flow; Lindeman's 10% ecological efficiency rule (90% lost as metabolic heat and respiration); Ecological pyramids of numbers, biomass, and energy.

topics.title: Biogeochemical Cycles and Nutrient Recycling
topics.description: Carbon cycle: Photosynthesis, cellular respiration, combustion, and greenhouse effect global warming; Nitrogen cycle: Nitrogen fixation by Rhizobium in legume root nodules and free-living Azotobacter, nitrification by Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter, assimilation, ammonification, and denitrification by Pseudomonas; Phosphorus cycle; Eutrophication of water bodies caused by synthetic fertilizer runoff.

topics.title: Environmental Degradation and Climate Resilience in Ethiopia
topics.description: Deforestation causes (firewood, agricultural expansion) and consequences in Ethiopian highlands; Soil erosion mechanisms, terracing, and contour ploughing; Land degradation and desertification; Impact of erratic rainfall and recurring droughts on pastoralist communities; Ethiopia's Green Legacy Initiative and national reforestation campaigns.

topics.title: Biodiversity Conservation and Protected Area Management
topics.description: In-situ conservation: National Parks of Ethiopia (Simien Mountains, Bale Mountains, Awash, Nechisar, Gambella), wildlife sanctuaries (Babille Elephant Sanctuary), biosphere reserves (Kafa coffee forest); Ex-situ conservation: Ethiopian Biodiversity Institute (EBI) genebanks, botanical gardens, and captive breeding programs; Economic and ecological value of preserving endemic genetic resources.

book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 1: Acid-Base Equilibria covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Acid-Base Concepts
topics.description: Arrhenius, Brønsted-Lowry, and Lewis theories of acids and bases; conjugate acid-base pairs, amphiprotic species.

topics.title: Ionic Equilibria of Weak Acids and Bases
topics.description: Water autoionization, Kw, pH, pOH, Ka and Kb dissociation constants, percent ionization.

topics.title: Common Ion Effect and Buffer Solutions
topics.description: Common ion effect, buffer action, Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, buffer capacity.

topics.title: Hydrolysis of Salts
topics.description: Hydrolysis of salts of strong/weak acid-base combinations and pH predictions.

topics.title: Acid–Base Indicators and Titrations
topics.description: Acid-base indicators, equivalents & normality (N1V1 = N2V2), titration curves, and equivalence point.

book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 2: Electrochemistry covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Oxidation-Reduction Reactions
topics.description: Oxidation and reduction definitions, oxidation numbers, balancing redox reactions using oxidation-number and half-reaction methods.

topics.title: Electrolysis of Aqueous Solutions
topics.description: Metallic vs electrolytic conduction, electrolytic cells, factors affecting preferential discharge, molten NaCl, brine, dilute H2SO4, CuSO4.

topics.title: Quantitative Aspects of Electrolysis
topics.description: Faraday's First and Second Laws of Electrolysis, electrochemical equivalent, charge and mass calculations.

topics.title: Industrial Application of Electrolysis
topics.description: Extraction of aluminum (Hall-Héroult), electrorefining of copper, electroplating, chlor-alkali production of Cl2 and NaOH.

topics.title: Voltaic Cells
topics.description: Daniell cell, salt bridge, standard hydrogen electrode (SHE), standard reduction potentials, Nernst equation, commercial batteries, fuel cells, and corrosion.

book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 3: Industrial Chemistry covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Introduction to Industrial Chemistry
topics.description: Scope, characteristics of chemical industries, role in society and economic growth.

topics.title: Natural Resources and Industry
topics.description: Atmospheric, hydrospheric, lithospheric, biospheric raw materials; renewable and non-renewable resources in Ethiopia.

topics.title: Manufacturing of Valuable Products/Chemicals
topics.description: Haber ammonia, Ostwald nitric acid, Contact sulfuric acid, Solvay sodium carbonate, Castner-Kellner NaOH, Urea and DAP fertilizers, pesticides.

topics.title: Some Manufacturing Industries in Ethiopia
topics.description: Glass, ceramics, cement, sugar refining, pulp and paper, tannery, food preservation, ethanol, soaps and detergents.

book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 4: Polymers covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Introduction to Polymers
topics.description: Monomers, polymers, degree of polymerization (DP), homopolymers and copolymers.

topics.title: Polymerization Reactions
topics.description: Addition (chain-growth) vs condensation (step-growth) polymerization; free-radical mechanisms; Nylon 6,6 and Dacron.

topics.title: Classification of Polymers
topics.description: Natural biopolymers (carbohydrates, proteins, nucleic acids, rubber) vs synthetic polymers (PE, PP, PVC, PMMA, Teflon); thermoplastics vs thermosets.

book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 5: Introduction to Environmental Chemistry covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Introduction and Components of the Environment
topics.description: Atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere, biosphere; hydrological, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, sulfur cycles; BOD, DO, TLV.

topics.title: Environmental Pollution
topics.description: Air pollution, photochemical smog, acid rain, CFCs ozone depletion; water pollution and eutrophication; land pollution.

topics.title: Global Warming and Climate Change
topics.description: Greenhouse gases (CO2, CH4, N2O), infrared absorption mechanism, and global climate impacts.

topics.title: Green Chemistry and Cleaner Production
topics.description: 12 principles of green chemistry, atom economy calculation, cleaner production goals in chemical industries.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 1: Academic Reading and Synthesizing Complex Information
book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 1: Academic Reading and Synthesizing Complex Information covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Academic Reading: Text Analysis, Tone and Main Ideas
topics.description: Skimming scholarly articles for main idea, scanning for supporting empirical data, evaluating author purpose and objective vs subjective tone, making logical inferences from academic prose, and distinguishing asserted facts from hypotheses.

topics.title: Scholarly Vocabulary: Affixation and Academic Word List
topics.description: Morphological word analysis: Latin and Greek prefixes (anti-, bio-, inter-, poly-, trans-) and suffixes (-tion, -ize, -ous, -able); Contextual collocations in university research papers; Connotative nuances of scholarly synonyms.

topics.title: Advanced Relative Clauses and Sentence Synthesis
topics.description: Defining vs non-defining relative clauses (comma rules, which vs that, who vs whom, whose); Reduced relative clauses (participle clauses using present -ing and past -ed participles); Combining simple sentences into cohesive compound-complex academic sentences.

topics.title: Speaking and Discussion: Academic Seminars and Debates
topics.description: Active listening during scholarly presentations, formulating constructive questions, discourse markers for polite disagreement ("While I acknowledge your point, evidence suggests..."), and summarizing group conclusions.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 2: Advanced Grammatical Structures for Entrance Examinations
book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 2: Advanced Grammatical Structures for Entrance Examinations covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Mastery of Conditional Sentences and Counterfactuals
topics.description: Zero, First, Second, and Third Conditionals review; Mixed conditionals (unreal past action with present consequence: If + past perfect, would + base verb); Formal inversion without 'if' ("Had I known the schedule...", "Were the committee to approve...", "Should you require assistance...").

topics.title: Advanced Passive Voice Constructions
topics.description: Passive with reporting verbs for academic objectivity ("It is widely believed that...", "The findings are said to indicate..."); Passive infinitive and gerund forms; Causative passive structures (have/get something done); Avoiding agent identification when agent is unknown or irrelevant.

topics.title: Reported Speech and Indirect Discourse
topics.description: Tense backshift rules in reported speech (simple present to simple past, present perfect to past perfect); Exceptions when reporting universal scientific truths; Reporting verbs with specific patterns (insist on, apologize for, deny + gerund, advise someone to do); Shifting time and place adverbs.

topics.title: Modals of Deduction, Speculation and Past Regret
topics.description: Present deduction (must be, can't be, might be); Past deduction and speculation (must have been, can't have done, might have seen); Expressing past obligation and regret (should have studied, ought to have submitted); Common multiple-choice distractors in national EUEE entrance exams.

book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 3: Scientific and Technical Writing covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Expository Writing: Process Descriptions and Technical Reports
topics.description: Structuring laboratory reports: Introduction, Materials & Methods (passive voice sequential instructions), Results, and Discussion; Sequential connectors (initially, subsequently, simultaneously, following this, ultimately); Precision and concise scientific prose.

topics.description: Water autoionization, Kw, pH, pOH, Ka and Kb dissociation constants, percent ionization.

topics.title: Common Ion Effect and Buffer Solutions

topics.title: Hydrolysis of Salts

topics.title: Acid–Base Indicators and Titrations

topics.title: Electrolysis of Aqueous Solutions
topics.description: Metallic vs electrolytic conduction, electrolytic cells, factors affecting preferential discharge, molten NaCl, brine, dilute H2SO4, CuSO4.

topics.title: Quantitative Aspects of Electrolysis
topics.description: Faraday's First and Second Laws of Electrolysis, electrochemical equivalent, charge and mass calculations.

topics.title: Industrial Application of Electrolysis

topics.title: Voltaic Cells
topics.description: Daniell cell, salt bridge, standard hydrogen electrode (SHE), standard reduction potentials, Nernst equation, commercial batteries, fuel cells, and corrosion.

topics.title: Some Manufacturing Industries in Ethiopia
topics.description: Glass, ceramics, cement, sugar refining, pulp and paper, tannery, food preservation, ethanol, soaps and detergents.

topics.title: Academic Reading: Text Analysis, Tone and Main Ideas
topics.description: Skimming scholarly articles for main idea, scanning for supporting empirical data, evaluating author purpose and objective vs subjective tone, making logical inferences from academic prose, and distinguishing asserted facts from hypotheses.

topics.title: Scholarly Vocabulary: Affixation and Academic Word List
topics.description: Morphological word analysis: Latin and Greek prefixes (anti-, bio-, inter-, poly-, trans-) and suffixes (-tion, -ize, -ous, -able); Contextual collocations in university research papers; Connotative nuances of scholarly synonyms.

topics.title: Advanced Relative Clauses and Sentence Synthesis
topics.description: Defining vs non-defining relative clauses (comma rules, which vs that, who vs whom, whose); Reduced relative clauses (participle clauses using present -ing and past -ed participles); Combining simple sentences into cohesive compound-complex academic sentences.

topics.title: Speaking and Discussion: Academic Seminars and Debates
topics.description: Active listening during scholarly presentations, formulating constructive questions, discourse markers for polite disagreement ("While I acknowledge your point, evidence suggests..."), and summarizing group conclusions.

book_chapters.chapter_title: Unit 2: Advanced Grammatical Structures for Entrance Examinations
book_chapters.description: Official Ethiopian Curriculum Unit 2: Advanced Grammatical Structures for Entrance Examinations covering foundational scientific principles, problem-solving derivations, and national entrance examination mastery.

topics.title: Mastery of Conditional Sentences and Counterfactuals
topics.description: Zero, First, Second, and Third Conditionals review; Mixed conditionals (unreal past action with present consequence: If + past perfect, would + base verb); Formal inversion without 'if' ("Had I known the schedule...", "Were the committee to approve...", "Should you require assistance...").

topics.title: Advanced Passive Voice Constructions
topics.description: Passive with reporting verbs for academic objectivity ("It is widely believed that...", "The findings are said to indicate..."); Passive infinitive and gerund forms; Causative passive structures (have/get something done); Avoiding agent identification when agent is unknown or irrelevant.

topics.title: Reported Speech and Indirect Discourse
topics.description: Tense backshift rules in reported speech (simple present to simple past, present perfect to past perfect); Exceptions when reporting universal scientific truths; Reporting verbs with specific patterns (insist on, apologize for, deny + gerund, advise someone to do); Shifting time and place adverbs.

topics.title: Modals of Deduction, Speculation and Past Regret
topics.description: Present deduction (must be, can't be, might be); Past deduction and speculation (must have been, can't have done, might have seen); Expressing past obligation and regret (should have studied, ought to have submitted); Common multiple-choice distractors in national EUEE entrance exams.
